subject: pe
title: Applications: SMART Goals & Feedback
welcome_lead: Set sharper goals and use feedback to sharpen performance.
meta_desc: GCSE PE Sport Psychology applications: SMART goals, types of feedback, guidance.
final_note: Top class! You can now set and refine training goals like a pro.

concepts.def: Goal targets a clear, exact outcome.
Progress can be tracked with numbers.
From within — how the movement felt.
Feedback on the outcome (did it go in?).

walkthroughs.body_html:
Compare these:

  • Weak: "I want to run faster."
  • SMART: "I will run 5 km in under 25 minutes within 8 weeks by training 3 times a week."

That is Specific (5 km), Measurable (time), Achievable, Realistic and Time-bound (8 weeks).

Intrinsic (kinaesthetic feel), extrinsic (coach, crowd), knowledge of results (outcome — did the kick score?), knowledge of performance (technique quality). Beginners need lots of extrinsic and KR; experts rely more on intrinsic.
Coaches use four guidance styles: visual (demo or video), verbal (instructions), manual (hands-on support like guiding a tennis swing) and mechanical (equipment like floats or harnesses).
